Package com.egradx.auth.config

Class EgradxPlatformBootstrap

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.auth.config.EgradxPlatformBootstrap
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.boot.ApplicationRunner, org.springframework.core.Ordered
public class EgradxPlatformBootstrap extends Object implements org.springframework.boot.ApplicationRunner, org.springframework.core.Ordered
Brings the platform into existence on first startup: the six authorities egradx-auth's own endpoints are gated by, the platform organization, its Admin role, and the one user who can log into it.

Every step is guarded by an existence check, so this is safe to run on every boot and safe against a half-finished previous run (a crash between creating the organization and creating its admin leaves a recoverable state, not a stuck one).

This is the only thing egradx-auth seeds. An application's own authority vocabulary and its own default roles are its business — see EgradxOrganizationCreatedEvent for where an app hooks into organization creation.

Runs at high precedence because Spring sorts ApplicationRunners and CommandLineRunners into one list: a host app's own seeder is very likely to carry an @Order, and an unordered runner sorts last, which would have this seeding the platform only after the application had already tried to use it. Host seeders should leave their order at anything lower-precedence than this, which any ordinary positive @Order value already is.
